title: Lock every element to an edge
before: Everything centered. Seven buttons wrap into a loose cloud, and no line runs from one block to the next.
after: The banner gives the card a new top edge, the avatar and the actions sit on one line, and each block meets two edges.

title: Keep related things close
before: The same list stretched across the whole screen. Every task sits a long way from its due date.
after: At its natural width, each task and its date read as one row.

title: Differentiate instead of spacing out
before: Six sentences at the same weight. Adding padding would only make the block taller.
after: Grouped by due date, with faces for people, chips for categories and the link color for links. You find any task in a second.

title: Show, don't tell
before: An info icon, a paragraph about how to read the report, one sentence per number, and a note explaining the note.
after: Bars you compare at a glance, with the one far over its average in amber. Exact values are one hover away.

title: Icon-only is for universal icons
before: Eight icons with no labels. You can't tell what any of them does until its tooltip shows up.
after: A count, three actions with labels, and icons only where everyone knows them: delete and more.

title: Emphasis is a difference
before: Every value is a blue chip, and every one is the default, so the color tells you nothing.
after: The defaults are quiet, so the one setting someone changed is the first thing you see.

title: Dissolve the cards
before: A box around a header box, four field boxes and a box of boxes: three radii and borders stacked on borders.
after: One column edge, sections split by thin lines, and color only on the value that's unusual.

title: Landing page: headline on top, the product in the kitchen
before: A badge, gradient text, a paragraph of buzzwords, three buttons and three icon cards. It could be selling anything.
after: A centered claim only this product can make and one action, then the week planner standing in a real kitchen, with the reorder it suggests at 5pm crossing its edge.

title: Landing page: type as big as the idea
before: A tracked-out label, half the headline in a gradient, a ticking countdown and a row of big numbers.
after: A specimen sheet: the name in a light weight across the full width, measured by guide lines on the font's real metrics, over a band of Porto's cobalt tiles with the facts and speakers.

title: Landing page: the product as a still life
before: A pastel gradient, emoji in the logo, a welcome headline, a paragraph about passion and three icon cards.
after: One loaf lit like a still life under a serif headline, the story and the action on the dark either side, and what's on the shelf right now along the bottom.

title: Landing page: dark, the output as the object
before: A purple glow, a glowing pill, gradient text, glass cards and claims anyone could make.
after: Dark because it lives next to a terminal. A centered headline with a real stake, then Seam's own report: real write traffic, replayed, with the 38-second hole the migration would punch in it.

title: Color is for meaning
before: A gradient background, a loud color on every card, and white text that's hard to read on them.
after: Neutral surfaces hold the structure, and color is saved for the data: storage by type.

title: Dark mode is built, not inverted
before: The light theme flipped: pure black, pure white text, borders you can't see, and an accent that buzzes.
after: Surfaces get lighter as they rise, text steps down from white, and the accent takes a lighter step of its ramp.

title: Destructive means red, and says what it does
before: The brand color on "Yes" makes removing things look like the normal path, and "Yes / No" sends you back to reread the question.
after: Red for the action you can't undo, a button that names it, and what you'll lose in one sentence.

title: Let the data decide the form
before: Every column is left-aligned plain text at the same weight.
after: Departments become chips, numbers line up on the right in tabular figures, long emails truncate, the inactive row fades, and only the unusual status gets color.

title: Events over time want a timeline
before: A table of timestamps you have to read cell by cell.
after: Order, who and what at a glance: faces, markers whose color means something, and dates the way people say them.

title: Show the right things, reveal the rest
before: Every row carries every action, so the list is mostly buttons, and Delete is always one click away.
after: Rows show the data. Frequent actions appear on hover with tooltips, and rare ones live in the menu.

title: The generated dashboard, and what it becomes
before: A greeting with an emoji, a sentence about the page, tracked capitals, icons in circles and a green pill on every number.
after: The page title, the numbers, and red on the one number that needs attention.

title: On a phone, rows stop being a table
before: The desktop table at 390 wide: tiny text, cut-off columns and a sideways scroll.
after: Two lines per row: who and how much, then the details and the status. Grouped by what needs attention, and easy to tap.
